notes: Target was portes cochères, pedestrian entrances, their ironwork, and -- critically -- the entrance seen IN CONTEXT beside period shopfronts so relative size can be read. Full-text Commons search on French terms ('porte cochere Paris immeuble XIXe', 'devanture boutique Paris XIXe fonte', 'porte cochère haussmannien', etc.) returned almost nothing but book/PDF scans (Balzac, Zola, La Cité, Rochegude's Promenades...) -- restricting to filetype:bitmap helped but most hits were still off-topic (Paris Métro train doors, unrelated 17th-18th c. Marais doorways). What actually worked was combing Category:Haussmannian architecture in Paris and Category:Balconies in Paris for named addresses, then pivoting to full-text searches on those specific streets/corners (avenue de l'Opéra, rue Halévy, boulevard des Capucines, rue Saint-Lazare, place d'Estienne d'Orves / rue de Châteaudun, rue de Rivoli, boulevard Voltaire) to find MOSSOT's and Roger-Viollet/Paris Musées' clean facade-level shots. Kept 9: (01) 23 avenue de l'Opéra 'Au Gagné Petit' -- a rusticated round-arch department-store entrance several storeys tall standing directly beside a run of cast-iron-framed shopfronts with a glazed iron canopy/marquise, the clearest 'entrance as ruler beside the shopfronts' read in the set (Lansiaux, CC0, photographed 1916 -- photo date only, building is part of the avenue's 1864-70s construction). (02) rue Halévy corner -- Commons title itself calls this 'Elévation type de la façade prévue dans le décret de 1860': round-arched pedestrian door with a single mascaron keystone directly beside a full cast-iron-framed shopfront (now Zara) at identical ground-floor datum, full comble/balcon-filant stack above -- about as canonical as the corpus gets. (03) Grand Hôtel, 15 boulevard des Capucines -- the arcaded former main entrance plus flanking shop bays (now 'Le Grand Hôtel Paris' / 'bonbon watch'), each round arch with a dense wrought-iron scrolled grille; Commons dates the Cavelier atlantes above the arcade to 'vers 1861/1862', which is a genuine sourced construction date, not a photo-capture date -- used as 'year'. (04) 27 rue Saint-Lazare -- a paired round-arched porte cochère (carriage-height, iron gate visible through the opening) and a matching pedestrian door with an ornamented cast-iron fanlight grille and a carved cartouche between them; unusually clean read of a genuine two-door entrance bay. (05) 2 place d'Estienne d'Orves / 60 rue de Châteaudun corner -- a deep-red double-leaf porte cochère flanked by carved telamon figures, directly beside a Café Brasserie 'La Rotonde' awning on one side and a bank shopfront on the other -- strong entrance-vs-shopfront size contrast (a second, more distant shot of the same corner, 'Immeuble 2 place d'Estienne d'Orves et 60 rue de Châteaudun 078', was reviewed and dropped as a near-duplicate, weaker angle). (06) 2 boulevard Voltaire -- a plain, unornamented wood double-leaf porte cochère beside a rolled steel shop shutter and a restaurant awning; the one 'ordinary register' entrance in the set, useful as a counterweight to the grand corner buildings that dominate what Commons has catalogued. (07) 53 rue Blanche -- a tall arched pale-green painted wood porte cochère with a plain moulded surround, beside a real-estate-agency shopfront; also used in the se-comble family for its roofline, reused here because it is simply the cleanest 'plain ordinary porte cochère beside a shop' read found. (08) 65 rue de Rivoli -- a dark green double-leaf door with carved herm/caryatid figures and a round oculus fanlight, sandwiched between two contemporary clothing-chain shopfronts at the same ground-floor datum -- rue de Rivoli's eastern stretch (this address) was pierced/built under the Second Empire (1852-57 Haussmann extension toward the Bastille), so the corner-shop-modernised ground floor still sits on a period carcass. (09) 38 avenue de l'Opéra -- kept as secondary/supporting evidence: a full shopfront row (Melville & Ziffer furriers, Agence des Théâtres) with its cast-iron canopy frame and the wrought-iron balcony band above reading 'Comptoir de Paris' -- no entrance door is visible in this one, it is here purely for the 'shopfronts of the period, cast-iron framing, larger panes' half of the brief. Rejected 17: two 'Cour d'immeuble avec porte cochère ouverte' shots at 21 and 25 rue Saint-Paul (4e) turned out, once viewed, to show a decrepit plain-rendered pre-Haussmann Marais courtyard tenement -- no ashlar, no balconies, wrong typology entirely, despite a promising title and a CC0 Paris Musées source; rue de l'Échiquier 21-29 'porte cochère' is boarded up with plywood and covered in graffiti, door itself is gone; Paris 75004 rue de Rivoli no 88 'door' has had its actual door removed and the arched opening turned into an H&M/Zara display window -- surround survives but there is no door or ironwork left to show; 88 avenue des Champs-Élysées (Guerlain flagship) is a documented 1914 building, decades past the cutoff; Immeuble 66bis rue du Faubourg-Montmartre is an explicit Art Nouveau ceramic-tile 'Hydrothérapie' shopfront, also far too late; P1250051 rue Parrot (12e) has bow-window/oriel turrets on both corners of the facade, which is one of the brief's own explicit post-1882 tells, and no entrance visible regardless; 32 rue de Châteaudun is a fully mascaron-and-cartouche-encrusted window register (every opening carries a carved head), the 'near-universal mascaron' over-ornament tell, and shows no entrance; Immeuble 16 rue Halévy / 13 rue de la Chaussée d'Antin is a rounded-corner tourelle with a domed roof -- a corner-dome tell -- and its ground floor is a fully modernised Etam store with aluminium-and-glass doors, nothing period-legible remains; 27, 34 avenue de l'Opéra plates from the same Lansiaux/PH20746-20748 series were reviewed (34 is a china-shop window display, no entrance) and not kept separately; 12 rue Sédillot and 3 square Rapp (7e, incategory grille search) are Champ-de-Mars quarter buildings from the 1890s-1900s, outside the period; Rue Réaumur 116 and rue Philippe-de-Girard 72bis ('porte cochère' in the title) sit in quarters (Sentier metal-frame district, La Chapelle) built up mostly after 1880; two Médiathèque-de-l'architecture 'Grille' plates at 34 quai de l'Hôtel-de-Ville show a wine-merchant's shopfront explicitly captioned '(1898?)' and a neighbouring plain rustic-plank service door of uncertain but likely pre-Haussmann date -- both dropped; 'Vue prise de la rue Vivienne' PH20717 is a distant, small, heavily-margined archival print with no legible facade detail; 'Rue de Rivoli, détail de façade' PH9943 turned out to be a close-up of a 1900s-1910s 'Défense d'afficher' poster strip, not architecture. Dating discipline: Commons extmetadata is a photo-capture date in nearly every case (2011, 2016, 2026, etc. for the modern digital shots; 1916 for the Lansiaux avenue-de-l'Opéra plates) and was never used as a building date -- 'year' is left blank throughout except image 03, where the Commons description itself independently states the Cavelier atlantes/facade sculpture date to 'vers 1861/1862', which is a sourced construction-era claim, not a capture-date proxy. 'klass' is my own visual read of scale/richness (shopfront + street register), not sourced. Coverage gap: no clean interior-courtyard shot of an open porte cochère survived review -- the one candidate found (rue Saint-Paul) was the wrong period; and every 'grand register' entrance found from Commons happens to sit on a corner or a boulevard frontage, so the set is corner/boulevard-heavy despite active searching for a mid-block example -- 06 and 07 are the only two counterweights toward the plain mid-block register.

images.shows: A tall rusticated round-arch entrance (department store 'Au Gagné Petit') standing several storeys high directly beside a long run of cast-iron-framed shopfronts under a glazed iron canopy/marquise -- the clearest single read in the set of the entrance's height and mass measured against the shopfronts and window bays either side of it.

images.title: Immeuble rue Halévy -- élévation type du décret de 1860
images.author: MOSSOT
images.shows: Round-arched pedestrian entrance with a single mascaron keystone set directly beside a full cast-iron-framed shopfront (now Zara) at the same ground-floor datum, with the complete balcon-filant / pedimented-dormer comble stack above -- Commons' own title calls this the model elevation prescribed by the 1860 decree.

images.title: Le Grand Hôtel, boulevard des Capucines
images.author: MOSSOT
images.shows: The Grand Hôtel's arcaded former main entrance and flanking shop bays, each round arch fitted with a dense wrought-iron scrolled grille, directly beside contemporary shopfronts at street level -- Commons dates the Jules Cavelier atlantes on the facade above the arcade to 'vers 1861/1862', an independently sourced construction date rather than a photo-capture date.

images.title: 27, rue Saint-Lazare
images.author: MOSSOT
images.shows: A paired entrance bay: a full carriage-height round-arched porte cochère (iron gate visible through the opening) beside a matching pedestrian door, both set under an ornamented cast-iron fanlight grille with a carved cartouche between them -- an unusually clean read of a genuine two-door Second Empire entrance and its ironwork.

images.title: 2, place d'Estienne d'Orves
images.author: MOSSOT
images.street: 2 place d'Estienne d'Orves / 60 rue de Châteaudun, Paris 9e
images.shows: A deep-red double-leaf porte cochère flanked by carved telamon figures, standing directly beside a café-brasserie awning on one side and a bank shopfront on the other -- a strong side-by-side contrast between the entrance's height and the shopfronts' more modest scale on the same ground floor.

images.title: 2, boulevard Voltaire
images.author: Lionel Allorge
images.shows: A plain, unornamented wood double-leaf porte cochère beside a rolled-steel shop shutter and a restaurant awning -- the one 'ordinary register' entrance kept in the set, a counterweight to the grand corner buildings that otherwise dominate what Commons has catalogued for this feature.

images.title: 53, rue Blanche
images.author: Pline
images.shows: A tall arched pale-green painted wood porte cochère with a plain moulded surround, directly beside a real-estate-agency shopfront -- full facade above shows the plain window surrounds, small pediments and continuous wrought-iron balconies of a restrained mid-register building; also used in the se-comble family for its roofline.

images.title: 65, rue de Rivoli
images.author: Neoclassicism Enthusiast
images.shows: A dark green double-leaf door with carved herm/caryatid figures and a round oculus fanlight, sandwiched between two contemporary shopfronts at the same ground-floor datum -- this stretch of rue de Rivoli was built as part of Haussmann's 1852-57 eastward extension of the street, so a period entrance survives even though the flanking shopfronts have been modernised.
